title: Grateful Dead Live at Radio City Music Hall on 1980-10-23
lineage: Cassette Master (Nakamichi DR-1/Dolby B) -> Sound Devices 744T (24bit/96k) -> Adobe Audition v1.5 -> Samplitude Professional v10.21 -> FLAC/16
source: (FOB) Sony ECM-280 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell UDXLII-C90/Dolby B)

ai_review.summary: Energetic performance highlighted by a crowd‑charged China Doll, but audience chatter makes the first set tough to enjoy.
ai_review.review: The show is praised for its high energy and a memorable moment when Jerry launches into "China Doll," sending the audience into a swell. However, several listeners note that persistent yelling from the crowd ("down in front", "sit down") muddies the first‑set listening experience, making the recording feel more like an audience capture than a clean soundboard feed.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviews are split between high praise (5 and 4 stars) for performance energy and strong criticism (1 and 0 stars) for intrusive audience noise, resulting in an overall average rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Frequent crowd shouting ('down in front', 'sit down') distracts from the music and creates a muddied mix, especially noticeable in the first set.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The concert maintains high energy overall, but the first set suffers from disruptive audience noise that hampers listening enjoyment.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His vocal on "China Doll" is highlighted as a crowd‑pleasing moment.
